note: Pila A = medible sin ambiguedad por texto/regex, umbral claro. Pila B = requiere juicio real, sin umbral objetivo. Solo la pila A tiene checker en dockerfile_checks.py.

rules.statement: Pin the image version to a specific digest or a non-latest tag to keep builds reproducible.
Always combine RUN apt-get update with apt-get install in the same RUN statement.
Clean the apt cache (rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*) in the same RUN statement that installs packages.
CMD should almost always be used in the exec form: CMD ["executable", "param1", "param2"].
Do not run the container as root when a non-root user can be used instead.
Avoid installing or using sudo due to unpredictable TTY and signal-forwarding behavior.
Always use absolute paths for your WORKDIR.
Use WORKDIR instead of proliferating instructions like RUN cd ... && do-something.
Use COPY for copying files; reserve ADD for remote URLs or local archives that need automatic extraction.
Prepend set -o pipefail && to RUN statements that use a pipe, so an upstream failure fails the build.
Use a .dockerignore file to exclude files not relevant to the build, even if they're in the same directory.
Split your Dockerfile into distinct stages so the final image only contains what's needed.
rules.why_not: Requiere juzgar si un proyecto concreto se beneficia de separar build-time de runtime; muchos Dockerfiles legitimos de una sola etapa no violan nada verificable.

rules.statement: Choose a minimal, trusted base image (Docker Official Images, Verified Publisher, or Docker-Sponsored Open Source).
rules.why_not: Determinar si una imagen base es 'confiable' o 'minima' requiere conocer el catalogo de publishers verificados y comparar tamanos, no es un patron de texto en el Dockerfile.

rules.statement: Each container should have only one concern; limiting to one process per container is a good rule of thumb.
rules.why_not: Es una guia arquitectonica ('good rule of thumb', no absoluta) que exige entender que hace cada proceso lanzado, no algo que un regex sobre RUN/CMD pueda decidir.

rules.statement: Rebuild your images regularly with updated dependencies and build/test them in CI.
rules.why_not: Es una practica operativa sobre el proceso de CI, no una propiedad que un Dockerfile puntual exprese en su texto.

rules.statement: Avoid switching USER back and forth frequently, since it adds layers.
rules.why_not: Contar instrucciones USER no distingue un cambio necesario (build user -> runtime user) de uno descuidado; requiere leer el proposito de cada etapa.

rules.statement: Add labels to help organize images by project, record licensing, and automate builds.
rules.why_not: No hay un conjunto fijo de labels exigidos; que labels agregar depende del proyecto y de convenciones externas al Dockerfile.

rules.statement: Use the common, traditional port for your application in EXPOSE.
rules.why_not: Sin saber que aplicacion corre el contenedor no hay forma de decidir cual es su puerto 'tradicional'.

rules.statement: Use VOLUME to expose database storage areas, configuration storage, or files created by the container.
rules.why_not: Identificar que directorios son estado persistente del servicio requiere conocer la aplicacion, no es deducible del Dockerfile solo.

rules.statement: Images built with ONBUILD should get a separate tag; be careful with ADD/COPY inside ONBUILD.
rules.why_not: Aplica solo a imagenes base para otros builds, un caso de uso minoritario que requiere contexto del proyecto para evaluar si corresponde.
